actual_scope: Can one hosted native word serve two copies of the chain-nested root at once, on separate main registers, so that the helpers are shared between the chains and the complete signed invoice improves?
scope_change_reason: Same hosted native, A6 declaration and BIT line as #6889. Changed: the root becomes two #6833 chain roots on orthogonal coordinates (t = 0, a reducible root), the caller gets one HOST2 contact per stage serving both chains, and the word carries four main registers per port (same-label second mains, 959 helpers, 38,334 events). Correctness rests on the exact replay of the final word and the root block identities. The BIT saving of the open #6726 (.00376669) is necessary: nothing else on main clears kappa + 4 gap. The logarithm power is written as 2134 (minimum 2133). Raw counts 963,421,184 / 965,490,968 / 971,071,328, all below 10^9. LAMBDA priced as ordinary work is a review question (paid rank 1 per port gives S < 0). Inherited: owned ascent (A6, 23 rises of mass 56, peak 30, 8 owned reads of Y2), LAMBDA and IDLE_ONE.
bottleneck_link: docs/research/research-family-status.md; complete signed native/caller invoice and all supplier-admission gates
stop_rule: The claim is conditional on the five retained framework assumptions, the declared owned ascent (A6), the BIT saving of the open #6726, and the declared new forms (reducible root, HOST2, same-label second mains); no claim above the pin; LAMBDA must be priced as ordinary work for any crossing to exist.
